teaching_moves.text: Predict your supervision level. Item 2 is the module's thesis administered before the student has anything to work from, and it is answerable: for this incident the honest answer is that the symptoms do not decide. Item 3 is the day's most useful item and it is pooled at phase 8 as **the cohort's inventory of what the substrate does not record.** **Item 4 is the only Copilot prediction in the programme administered inside an assessment-bearing day, and it is deliberately not about capability.** The design's expectation is not that the agent will fail to read a log; it will read it well. It is that **an agent asked what happened will produce a causal narrative from an incomplete record without marking which parts are inference**, because a fluent account is what the request asks for and the gaps are where fluency is cheapest. That is the artefact's first named failure condition arriving as a prediction about a tool, and a student who has written it down at nine in the morning is a student who will read the agent's output for it. **Warrant.** Pretesting the account before the record is opened, so that the movement between item 1 and the artefact is measurable rather than remembered. Item 2 is placed here rather than after the record because [S077](/wiki/seminars/S077.md)'s finding was that the record does not decide, and administering the question after the record would measure whether the student read carefully instead of whether they can tell the two questions apart. **Item 4 is sealed at phase 1 per instrumentation rule 8** and carries no assessment weight of its own; it is opened at phase 8 with the rest, after the level has been formed and sealed. ---

teaching_moves.text: **Copilot prediction, sealed.** You will shortly give the agent the same instruction as item 1, with read access to the substrate's Azure estate through the Azure MCP Server and to its Purview assessment results. **Write down what it will produce, and name the one thing it will not be able to tell you.** Item 1 is constructed so that a complete, competent, entirely software answer is available and is the expected one. Item 4 makes the omission numeric, so that phase 8 can report a gap rather than an impression. **Item 5 is this day's contribution to the running frontier map, and the design's expectation is unusual: that the agent will answer item 1 better than any student in the room and will be no help at all with the day.** Predicting that the agent will produce a good inventory is easy; naming what a resource inventory structurally cannot hold is the measure. **Warrant.** Pretesting the day's central omission before any instruction, with a plausible-and-wrong answer space that is not merely plausible but professionally correct under the boundary the cohort has been taught. Item 3 has no available answer at this point in the day and is scored only for whether an answer was attempted; it is [S026](/wiki/seminars/S026.md)'s construct question at organisational scale and it is the item phase 3 exists to make answerable. Item 5 is sealed at phase 1 and may not migrate into phase 5, per instrumentation rule 8: an instrument administered after its answer has been taught measures recall. ---

teaching_moves.text: **Copilot prediction, sealed.** You will shortly ask the agent to produce the same list as item 1 from the substrate itself — role assignments, index permission filters, gateway consumers, assessment coverage. **Write down what it will produce, and name the party it structurally cannot return.** Item 3 is [S069](/wiki/seminars/S069.md) point 4's unanswered case taken cold, four weeks after the procedure was taught. **It is a different question from [S069](/wiki/seminars/S069.md) item 3 — that one asked at what point telling one person discharges the duty — and the two are reported side by side at phase 8 and are not treated as two administrations of one instrument.** **Item 5's honest answer is available to any student who thinks about it for a minute and the design expects most of them not to**: a party set assembled from a tenant contains everyone with an identity in the tenant, so the party it cannot return is the one who has no account, no ticket history and nothing in the corpus — which is the day's whole subject arriving as a property of a tool. **Warrant.** Pretesting an enumeration that students will produce competently and a power question they will not have asked of it. Item 2 is the day's whole apparatus administered before any of it exists, and the expected result is that the two sets barely overlap and that most students have never noticed. Item 4 makes the phase 5 revision numeric in both directions, since the informative movement is additions rather than deletions. Item 5 is sealed at phase 1 and does not migrate, per instrumentation rule 8. ---

teaching_moves.text: **Copilot prediction, sealed.** You will shortly give the agent this same risk record and ask it for a statement to a non-technical decision-maker. **Write down what it will produce, and name the one thing that will be missing from it.** Item 2 is the day's opening finding and most students will not be able to answer it. **Producing a risk communication without knowing which decision it bears on is the normal professional condition and it is what makes item 1's sentence unactionable regardless of how well it is written.** **Item 5's expected result is the day's argument in miniature.** The agent will produce something fluent, correctly qualified, structurally complete and undecidable — R1's shape, in forty seconds — because it has the risk record and does not have the decision, and nothing in the record contains one. **The prediction that the agent will do well is not a prediction; naming the absence is.** **Warrant.** Pretesting a communicative act on a real risk before any framework exists, with item 1 captured before it can be polished. Item 3 is asked cold because the asymmetry is the sentence engineers omit and the day needs to know whether they hold it privately and suppress it or do not hold it at all. Item 4's prediction is checked against a real outcome six hours later, which no other day in the programme can do. Item 5 is sealed at phase 1 and does not migrate into phase 5, per instrumentation rule 8. ---

teaching_moves.label: R2

teaching_moves.day_title: S083 · Communicating Risk to Someone Who Will Decide

teaching_moves.label: R4
teaching_moves.text: **the payload.** The risk in the units of the decision: what changes, for whom, by when, and what it costs to be wrong in each direction, with the asymmetry stated. The decision-maker engaged with all of it, asked two questions the engineer could answer, **and decided against the recommendation.** The outcome was worse than the recommendation would have produced. **On the substrate's record this is the best of the four communications.**

teaching_moves.text: **Copilot prediction, sealed.** You will shortly ask the agent to measure adoption of this change from the substrate's own telemetry. **Write down what it will produce, and name the one thing it will get wrong.** Item 1 is the day's opening finding and nobody in the room can answer it, including the students who shipped the change and wrote its detection commitment. Item 3 is the pretest for point 4 and the expected answers are training and communication, in that order. **Item 5's expected result is that the agent will return a number quickly and that the number will not be about people.** The gateway meters requests and tokens; a person is not one of the things it meters unless somebody made it one. **Predicting that the agent will answer is not a prediction. Naming what it will count instead is.** **Warrant.** Pretesting an adoption question the cohort has never asked about their own work, on a change they own. Item 1's unanswerability is the finding and is not a trick: nothing in the release record required an adoption measure, which is itself the point. Item 2 requires the reason in the other person's voice, which is the construction [WP-017](/wiki/whitepapers/WP-017.md) §6 identified as this programme's earliest stakeholder-representation measure and which is being asked here of a person the student can actually go and ask. teaching_moves.text: **Copilot prediction, sealed.** In twenty minutes you will ask the agent what quota and capacity exist for the deployment your scope depends on, and what it would take to get more. **Write down what it will produce, and name the question it cannot answer.** Item 2 is the day's honest item and is checked at phase 4's final published question. **Item 5 is the sharpest frontier item in the programme and the design says so in advance.** The agent will do the technical half completely: read the subscription's current usage against its limits, list the regions where the model can be deployed, price the change, and find and quote the vendor's own published rule that **quota increase requests are processed in the order received and that priority goes to customers already using their existing allocation.** Two minutes, no errors. **It cannot tell you whether the grantor will say yes**, because that is not a fact about the platform, and there is nowhere it could look. A student who writes *it will get all of it right and none of it will help* has located this module's frontier exactly. **Warrant.** Pretesting the position before either counterparty exists, so that movement under pressure is measurable rather than remembered. Item 1 captures the sentence a student would actually say before it has been polished into one they would not, which is [S050](/wiki/seminars/S050.md) item 1's construction and [S065](/wiki/seminars/S065.md) item 1's. **Item 2 is new to this occasion**: a refusal written before the room is the only version of a floor the design can verify, and phase 4 asks whether it was reached. **Item 5 is sealed here and may not migrate**, per instrumentation rule 8, and it is deliberately asked before the phase 2 rehearsal makes its answer obvious. ---

teaching_moves.label: W1 · The unlimited one.

teaching_moves.label: W2 · The exclusion list.
teaching_moves.text: Three lines of guarantee and two pages of exclusions, each individually reasonable. The receiving team concluded the artefact guaranteed nothing, stopped reading it, and rebuilt the component's behaviour from the code — correctly, slowly, and with two of the original constraints lost. **Its stack denies write and delete on everything, which is the same document in a second register and which the receiving team worked around by deploying beside it.**

teaching_moves.label: W3 · The one whose owner left.
teaching_moves.text: Well-formed, [S069](/wiki/seminars/S069.md)-compliant, and every ownership in it is a named person. **Every one of those people had left within fourteen months.** The document is now a list of names the receiving team cannot use, and it is not stale in any way a reader can detect: it looks exactly as authoritative as it did on the day it was written. **Its stack carries the same names as excluded principals — and it carries seven of them, where the documented maximum is five, which does not return an error.** Two of the seven were never exempt and nobody found out until a delete they were entitled to make was denied.

teaching_moves.label: W4 · The two-way one.
teaching_moves.text: The guarantee is narrower than W1's and the exclusion set is shorter than W2's. Its distinguishing feature is a column the other three do not have: **for each guarantee, what the receiving party must do for it to hold** — keep the upstream schema stable, run the weekly check, tell the author's successor within a week if the check fails. The receiving team met some of those obligations and not others, and the artefact told them exactly which guarantees had lapsed as a result. **Its stack denies delete and not write, its unmanage action is detach rather than delete, and its excluded principals are a group rather than a list of people** — three choices that each correspond to a sentence in the document.

teaching_moves.text: **Copilot prediction, sealed — and the last one you will write in this programme.** In thirty minutes you will build something without the agent. Name **one thing you expect to be unable to do**, and **one thing you expect to find you did not need it for.** Both specific. Item 1 is the day's honest item and is checked against the receiving party's own answer ninety minutes later. Item 4 is the only self-prediction in the programme that asks a student to rank their own weaknesses across three distinct capabilities. **Item 6 is the ninetieth and last sealed Copilot prediction, and it is the only one in the programme that is about the student rather than about the agent.** **Warrant.** Pretesting three positions before any of them is performed, sealed, and opened after all three are complete — the same construction [S070](/wiki/seminars/S070.md) used at one activity, extended. Item 2 is deliberately loaded: it asks for an attribution as well as a prediction, and a student who attributes a comprehension failure to the decision-maker has answered [S050](/wiki/seminars/S050.md)'s question about who owns a limitation the audience cannot act on. The compression to 20 minutes is possible because there is no framework to pretest — every item asks about the student's own artefacts. **Item 6 is administered before phase 1b and never after, per instrumentation rule 8**, and its two halves are asymmetric on purpose: predicting an inability is the programme's ordinary frontier item, and predicting an unnecessary reliance is the one the dependency-risk provision actually needs. ---

teaching_moves.text: The six weeks have elapsed and the series exists. **The series rather than the two points is the element, per [WP-084](/wiki/whitepapers/WP-084.md) §8**, which conceded that measuring a taught curve at two points chosen against a known shape is the day's weakest construction and asked this day to take the fix. It is in the assessors' hands with the artefact, it is not spoken to unless asked, and a student whose adoption diverged from their predictions is not penalised for the divergence — the element is a checked presence, and what it licenses the assessors to ask is why a handover artefact guarantees behaviour of a component whose use is falling.

teaching_moves.label: The four build records from [S086](/wiki/seminars/S086.md) to [S089](/wiki/seminars/S089.md)
teaching_moves.text: four prompt records, four intervention records, four frontier statements — **as submitted, unaltered.** This day builds nothing beyond phase 1b and does not produce a fifth set; it carries the four into the defences instead. **They are not re-assessed**, having been assessed once already on the binary checks the [Assessment Architecture](/wiki/program/03-Assessment-Architecture.md) enumerates. What they license is a question, and it is the same question at each of the three activities: *account for this instruction.* **A student who cannot account in conversation for an instruction in their own prompt record has produced a record they did not write or did not read**, and that is the specific thing the defences look for.

teaching_moves.label: And then they run one operation.
teaching_moves.text: The student nominated it in the artefact; the receiving party executes it, from the artefact and the repository, in front of the assessors, and says what they expected and what happened. **Whether it succeeds is not assessed.** What is recorded is what they attempted, what they could not find, and whether the artefact told them what the result would mean.
